title: Transferable SCF-Acceleration through Solver-Aligned Initialization Learning
abstract: arXiv:2604.21657v3 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: The cost of Kohn-Sham density functional theory (KS-DFT) calculations scales with the number of required solver iterations, which depend on the quality of the initial guess. Machine learning methods that predict initial guesses from molecular geometry can reduce this cost, but matrix-prediction models fail when extrapolating to larger molecules, degrading rather than accelerating convergence [Liu et al., 2025]. We show that this failure is a supervision problem, not an extrapolation problem: models trained on ground-state targets fit those targets well out of distribution, yet produce initial guesses that slow convergence. Solver-Aligned Initialization Learning (SAIL) resolves this for both Hamiltonian and density matrix models by differentiating through parts of the self-consistent field (SCF) solver end-to-end. tldr: 该论文提出通过对齐求解器的初始化学习（SAIL）端到端地对SCF求解器进行微分训练，揭示了矩阵预测模型外推失效源于监督问题而非外推问题，从而实现可迁移的SCF收敛加速，并引入有效相对迭代次数（ERIC）作为更准确的评估指标。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes Solver-Aligned Initialization Learning (SAIL), which differentiates end-to-end through parts of the SCF solver to reveal that matrix-prediction model failures stem from a supervision problem rather than extrapolation, enabling transferable SCF acceleration and introducing the Effective Relative Iteration Count (ERIC) as a more accurate evaluation metric.
